Noro said:

hey y'all im new here. Im a graduate student in econ and i want to get into financial econometrics/ML, is lean for me? I have some experience with python, R and C

Those language you mentioned are very different ( C kind of sticks out in that list as being fundamentally different to the others).

It depends , for practical application you probably should not switch to Lean, even though this is not impossible to do with Lean.

However if your concern is less about code safety, and you don’t care about the chance of run time errors , it wouldn’t necessarily make sense to implement it via Lean.

If you want to formally verify theorems about ML and econometrics, rather than run any such things as binary on a lot of data in application , Lean is more suitable than the others IMO.
